ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: On the left side of the circuit there are four inputs A, B, C, D, and on the right side there are four outputs W, X, Y, Z. The A path is directly connected to output W. In the figure there are three logic gates with XOR gate symbols: the first receives A and B, and outputs X; the second receives B and C, and outputs Y; the third receives C and D, and outputs Z. Reasoning: Therefore the output equations of the circuit are W = A, X = A ⊕ B, Y = B ⊕ C, Z = C ⊕ D. If ABCD is the original 4-bit binary number, then the standard binary-to-Gray-code conversion is exactly that the most significant bit remains unchanged, and each subsequent bit equals the XOR of adjacent binary bits, namely G = A, A⊕B, B⊕C, C⊕D. Therefore this circuit generates Gray code.
